chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Habib, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who bought a slave from another man, and the seller had two slaves. He said to the buyer, 'Go with them and choose whichever you wish, and return the other,' and the money had already been taken. The buyer took both, but one of them ran away (abqa) from him. He said: 'The one who has the other (the one that stayed) should return half of the price that he gave to the seller, and go in search of the slave. If he finds him, he chooses whichever he wishes and returns the half that he took. If he does not find him, the slave is shared between them; half is for the seller and half is for the buyer.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling when a purchased slave runs away before the buyer chooses which one to keep?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the ruling for a conditional sale where the buyer holds two slaves to choose from, establishing that if one escapes before selection, the buyer retains half the price and the remaining slave, while the seller retains the other half of the price. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of shared risk (ghurm) in incomplete transactions, ensuring equitable restitution based on the actual possession and value at the time of loss. It serves as a foundational precedent for modern commercial contracts involving conditional delivery and risk allocation.
